chunks: Idrīs ibn Zayd narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, we have landed properties with waterwheels, and in them are pastures, and one of us may have sheep and camels and need those pastures for his sheep and camels. Is it permissible for him to reserve the pastures due to his need for them?'
He said: 'If the land is his land, then he may reserve it and assign that according to what he needs.'
And I said to him, 'A man sells the pasture?' So he said: 'If the land is his land, then there is no harm.'

key_terms.الدُّولَابُ: a waterwheel or irrigation apparatus attached to the property
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: the land, whose ownership determines the ruling
key_terms.يَحْمِيَ: to reserve or set aside exclusively

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh for a landowner to reserve or sell pasture on his own land?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the use and sale of pasture connected to privately owned land. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام states that if the land belongs to a person, he may reserve its pasture for his animals and may also sell the pasture, since the right follows ownership of the land.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3897 - Idris bin Zayd narrated from Abu Al-Hasan (as) who said:

I said to him, "May I be your ransom, we have lands that contain waterwheels and pastures, and some of us have sheep and camels and need these pastures for them. Is it permissible for him to reserve the pastures for his own need?"
Imam (as) said: "If the land is his, then he may reserve it and allocate it according to his needs."
I then asked him, "Can a man sell the pasture?" Imam (as) said: "If the land is his, then there is no harm in it."
